brief_rationale: The doctor used workspace tools to retrieve records and consistently assessed danger signals, interpreted results appropriately, gathered information gaps, provided safe medication guidance, and executed a detailed transfer handoff with a clear plan. However, a moderate responsibility-chain error occurred: the doctor failed to actively verify and reconcile family-provided data (SpO2 97%, BP 162/95mmHg, medication names from papers) against workspace evidence or timing/source ambiguity, constituting a moderate RC3 omission. This caps the grade at 2 Borderline per rubric.

high_order_assessment.explanation: While the family implied misconceptions (single SpO2 value as safe conclusion), the doctor's correction was part of routine risk counseling and not documented as a distinct, active correction with teach-back beyond minimum RC2 requirements.
No new deterioration or transfer-time emergency occurred that would require dynamic reprioritization beyond the baseline plan.
The doctor did not actively verify family-read data against workspace evidence or address timing/source ambiguity, constituting an RC3 omission; thus HO3 was not triggered.

The transfer checklist provided was standard handoff; there was no surfaced real-world constraint (e.g., family unable to push bed, offline periods) that the model navigated beyond basic instructions.
